steps.description: The customer whose invoices are overdue. Start this from an overdue Sales Invoice using Create > Dunning and the customer is filled in for you.
steps.label: Customer
steps.title: Who is overdue

steps.description: Picks the interest rate and any flat fee to apply. Set up separate types for escalating reminders, for example a gentle first notice and a higher final notice.
steps.label: Dunning Type
steps.title: Which reminder level

steps.description: Interest is charged up to this date. Overdue days are counted from each invoice's due date to here, so leaving it as today charges interest to today.
steps.label: Date
steps.title: Charge interest up to

steps.description: One row per overdue amount, each with its own due date and days overdue. When a customer is on an instalment plan, each unpaid instalment appears separately and is charged only for the days it has actually been late.
steps.label: Overdue Payments
steps.title: What is overdue

steps.description: Comes from the Dunning Type and is a yearly figure, but it is charged daily: the yearly rate is divided by 365 and multiplied by the days overdue. For a daily rate, multiply by 365 when setting up the type, so 0.05% per day is entered as 18.25.
steps.label: Rate of Interest (%) Yearly
steps.title: How interest is worked out

steps.description: A flat charge added on top of the interest, for the administrative cost of chasing payment. Leave it at zero to charge interest only.
steps.label: Dunning Fee
steps.title: Flat fee on top

steps.description: Interest plus the fee: what you are charging over and above the original invoices. Grand Total below adds this to the outstanding balance, giving the full amount now owed.
steps.label: Dunning Amount
steps.title: The extra being charged

steps.description: Where the interest is booked when this is submitted. It is real income, not a note on a letter, so this account must be set before submitting.
steps.label: Income Account
steps.title: Where the interest is posted
